subject: INLAjoint - sharing a frailty with longitudinal mixed model

messages.author: eaed3c9567ed5c07
messages.subject: INLAjoint - sharing a frailty with longitudinal mixed model
parts:
I am checking whether it is possible to share a frailty term in a recurrent events model with a linear mixed model (which includes a random intercept) using INLAjoint? i.e. 

h_ik(t) = h_0(t) exp(B_0 + B_1 x_i + u_i) 
y_ij(t) = A_0 + A_1 t_ij + A_2 x_i + gamma u_i + v_i 

where x_i is a baseline binary covariate, u_i is a frailty and v_i a random intercept. 

I have read what I can find about the "SRE" and "SRE_ind" association options but am still unsure - any insights gratefully received. 

Many thanks, Keith

messages.author: 953deaf1a512b96e
messages.subject: Re: INLAjoint - sharing a frailty with longitudinal mixed model
parts:
Hi Keith,

This is not directly feasible with INLAjoint, but we can setup a model without that shared term with INLAjoint and then manually add it to fit the model with INLA. I made an example in the attached code for you.

Best,
Denis Rustand

parts:
Hi Denis,

many thanks for your previous advice - really do appreciate it!! 

I am also trying to replicate what you did for the biomarker and recurrent events model, but for a standard biomarker and terminal event (death) model so that I can get the variance-covariance matrix for the fixed effects, but I am struggling to know exactly how to update the formula (please see below and queries in RED) - could you offer any advice? 

Many thanks, Keith 

>>>
M3c <- joint(formLong = bm ~ obstimes + obstimes:AT + (1|id),
            dataLong = STUDY.df, id = "id", timeVar = "obstimes",
            formSurv = inla.surv(stime, dead) ~ AT,
            dataSurv = STUDY.id.df, assoc="", basRisk = "rw2",
            family=c("normal"))
summary(M3c)

M3cidata <- M3c$.args$data
M3cidata$IDIntercept_S1_L1 <- M3cidata$IDIntercept_L1 # Not sure if this correct (almost certainly isn't!) ??? 
M3ciformula <- update(M3c$.args$formula, "~ . ????")
M3c$.args$control.fixed$correlation.matrix=TRUE
M3c$.args$control$correlation.matrix=TRUE

# Run model directly in INLA to get covariance matrix
M3ci <- inla(M3ciformula, family = M3c$.args$family, data=M3cidata,
           control.fixed = M3c$.args$control.fixed,
           control.family = M3c$.args$control.family,
           control.predictor=M3c$.args$control.predictor, offset=M3c$.args$offset,
           control.compute=M3c$.args$control.compute,
           E = M3c$.args$data$E..coxph,
           control.inla = M3c$.args$control)
summary(M3ci)


#######################################

messages.author: 953deaf1a512b96e
messages.subject: Re: INLAjoint - sharing a frailty with longitudinal mixed model
parts:
Hi Keith,

If I understand you want to share the random intercept from the biomarker in the survival model for a terminal event? Or you still want to have a random effect in the survival model that is shared in the biomarker model?

In case you want to share the random intercept in the survival model, this can be done directly with INLAjoint, I just added the option to compute the correlation matrix of fixed effects, so you'll have to update INLAjoint to the latest GitHub version:

devtools::install_github('DenisRustand/INLAjoint', build_vignettes = TRUE)

Then the attached code shows how to get the correlation matrix. 

On the other hand, if you want to have a frailty term in the survival model shared in the biomarker model (as before), you'll need to keep the (1|id) in the survival formula and the formula update should be the same as in the first code.

Best,
Denis
